quests.title: The Strip Outside Emu Plains
quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. Nobody planted the strip at Emu Plains. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I did, on the long weekend, at five in the morning, so nobody would ask. I would like the fifteenth to go badly for council. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: the strip, which is a garden now
the man with the whipper snipper
photograph it while it still exists

quests.title: Night Fill, Schofields
quests.blurb: I would do it myself if I could leave the counter. Started on the long weekend. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. In off the Schofields late train, gone before the first delivery, every time, and it has been like that since the merge. Come in on the late one and watch the loading door. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: come in on the late one like they do
the loading door nobody watches
whoever is standing in it at two in the morning
$75 of what they took, back

quests.title: The Window Above Macdonaldtown
quests.blurb: Nobody else has offered, so. I live above the platform at Macdonaldtown and I know this line by sound. Half the street knows and half the street is pretending not to. Something in the rhythm changed about a month ago and everyone I tell thinks I am mad. Ride it and tell me whether I am mad. Ask for me by name at the counter.

steps.label: ride it and listen to the joins
photograph the stretch that sounds wrong
tell me I am not mad

quests.title: Setting Up at Epping
quests.blurb: You will think I am making this up. 21 years in the Epping market. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. The bays are not allocated, they are *known*, and since grand final week somebody has decided that knowing does not count, and nobody upstairs wants to hear it. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: the bays, at the hour it happens
the bloke with the extra trestle
you will want one at that hour
$56 of frontage, recovered

quests.title: The Clock at Sefton
quests.blurb: It has been three weeks. The clock on the Sefton platform has been four minutes fast since I got here and every relief who comes through wants to fix it. I have rung the number on the letter four times. Do not fix it. Find out who set it that way, before they retire. Do not make a scene about it.

steps.label: the clock, four minutes fast, for the file
to Chester Hill, where the old crew drink
bring the name back

quests.title: The Dog at Castle Hill
quests.blurb: I am told you do odd jobs. A dog meets the 5:40 at Castle Hill every weekday and nobody gets off for it. I am aware how that sounds. Four months of this. I have decided it is not going to be a sad story. Find out whose it is. I will know if you skipped a bit.

steps.label: the end of the platform, at twenty to six
the collar, if it has got one
the street it walks home to
tell me it is not a sad story

quests.title: The Book at Cabramatta
quests.blurb: The council knows and the council does not care. I run a small book on things that are not races — weather, delays, whether the quarter to six out of Cabramatta runs on time. I am not after trouble. I am after an answer. Somebody is beating it by information, not luck. Ride the run they ride. Come back and tell me straight.

steps.label: ride the run they ride
the two who follow you off it
$42 back off the book

quests.title: Last Service out of Burwood
quests.blurb: I have been putting it off since Easter. The last one through Burwood carries four people and one of them is always asleep. Nobody else seems to have noticed, which is its own problem. Ride it to Strathfield, photograph the platform with nobody on it, and come back and tell me the place still exists when there is no one in it. Do that and we're square.

steps.label: ride the late one to Strathfield
the empty platform, lit and pointless
tell them what you saw

quests.title: The Wiley Park Tap-Off
quests.blurb: Two people have already said no. A card ending 22 boards at Wiley Park on school holidays and vanishes. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Not a fare thing — ninety cents. I want to know *how*, and I have stopped filling in the form. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

steps.label: ride the run the card rides
the gap in the fence everyone knows about
photograph it before somebody welds it

quests.title: The Flemington Order
quests.blurb: Two people have already said no. I have made the same order for the same person every morning since I opened at Flemington. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Since every second Friday they have not turned up, and they keep sending a different bloke. Go and knock. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

steps.label: order one at the Flemington kiosk
the office they walk to, or used to
come back with $76 — I am not running a charity

quests.title: Four Minutes at Windsor
quests.blurb: This is going to sound small. The board at Windsor says four minutes. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. It has said four minutes since before the merge and it is a lie about a third of the time. Stand under it, time it, and bring me numbers instead of feelings. Do not make a scene about it.

steps.label: stand under the board and wait like everyone else
photograph the board saying four minutes
ride the one that finally comes
give me the number

quests.title: Unclaimed at Oatley
quests.blurb: This is going to sound small. Everything anyone leaves on the Oatley line ends up in a room and the room is full. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. Nine hundred umbrellas and one a clipboard nobody signed with a name on it and a number that rings out. Go to the address on the tag. Do not make a scene about it.

steps.label: the address on the tag
the two who got there before you
$53 — whatever it is, it is worth that to somebody

quests.title: The Quiet Carriage, Westmead
quests.blurb: I have written it down twice and lost it twice. The quiet carriage runs on shame and somebody on the knock-off out of Westmead has stopped feeling it. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Ride it, see the crime, and apply the shame manually. Ask for me by name at the counter.

steps.label: ride the quiet carriage and observe the crime
apply the shame manually
photograph the sign, for the record

quests.title: The Rozelle Bay Shortcut
quests.blurb: My knees are gone, so. Every courier has a route that is not on a map and mine goes through Rozelle Bay. I would not ask if there was anyone else about. They have started locking one end. Go and find out whether it is locked forever or just locked today. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

steps.label: the end they lock
the long way round, so you understand what it costs
$64, which is what the long way costs me a week

quests.title: Possession at Glenfield
quests.blurb: Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Third time at Glenfield on school holidays. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. Not kids — kids run. This one walks, and they keep sending a different bloke. I need it stopped before somebody writes a very long report about me. Do not make a scene about it.

steps.label: where they come through the fence
the ones who think a hard hat is a costume
photograph the gap so I can put a number on the form
